answer:
Data-grounded hypothesis (DiscoveryBench submission format; final natural-language hypothesis, no fabricated Black advantage).

(1) RAW / DESCRIPTIVE finding — answering the question as literally asked:

"At no SES level do Black students in the NLS sample (N = 8,773; 236 BA completions) hold a completion-rate advantage over White students. Across full-sample SES terciles, quartiles, quintiles, and a ±1 SD split, Black completion rates are at or below White completion rates in every stable cell. The Black–White gap is most pronounced at the LOW end of the SES distribution — Black 0.44% (Wilson 95% CI [0.17, 1.13]) versus White 3.05% [2.23, 4.16], a gap of −2.61 pp (race-stratified bootstrap 95% CI [−3.75, −1.57]). The gap narrows monotonically with rising SES but never reverses: −1.67 pp [−2.98, −0.40] in the middle tercile and −1.59 pp [−3.15, +0.16] in the upper tercile. Statistically, the gap is distinguishable from zero in the bottom two terciles and becomes indistinguishable only at the top of the distribution, where cell sizes are smallest (Black N=405 with 9 events)."

(2) REFRAMED / COVARIATE-ADJUSTED finding (robustness sanity check only) — explaining the question's presumed advantage:

"After conditioning on academic-resource composition (ASVAB ability composite, percentile in class, family size, sex) within SES bins, a Simpson-style reversal appears: Black students at mid and high SES complete BAs at higher adjusted-prediction rates than White students at the same SES tier, with the within-bin conditional Black advantage most pronounced at the MIDDLE-SES tier (logistic race × SES interaction +1.26 log-odds, SE = 0.62, p = 0.042; adjusted-prediction gap +5.3 pp, Black 9.33% vs White 3.99%). This conditional advantage is real in the conditional sense but it is masked in the raw, observational data by the fact that Black students reaching higher SES enter those bins with stronger measured academic resources than their White bin-mates."

(3) Single-sentence headline:

"In the NLS, the raw Black–White BA-completion gap is largest at low SES and persists (narrowing toward statistical indistinguishability) at higher SES; conditioning on academic-resource composition reverses the sign at mid and high SES, with the conditional Black advantage strongest at middle SES."

payload.hypothesis: At no SES level do Black students in the NLS sample hold a BA-completion rate advantage over White students in the raw, descriptive data. The Black–White gap is largest at low SES (Black 0.44% vs White 3.05%; gap -2.61 pp, bootstrap 95% CI [-3.75, -1.57]) and narrows monotonically with rising SES but never reverses; statistical distinguishability dissipates only at the top tercile (gap -1.59 pp [-3.15, +0.16]). This pattern is robust across terciles, quartiles, quintiles, and a ±1 SD split. Once academic-resource composition (ASVAB composite, percentile in class, family size, sex) is conditioned on, a within-bin Simpson-style reversal emerges, with a conditional Black advantage strongest at MIDDLE-SES (interaction +1.26 log-odds, p=0.042; adjusted-prediction gap +5.3 pp, Black 9.33% vs White 3.99%). Reframing the question literally: the raw SES-conditional completion-rate gap most disfavors Black students at low SES, while the academic-resource-conditional completion-rate gap most favors Black students at mid SES.
payload.workflow: Load data/nls_ses_processed.csv (N=8773; no missing values on race, SES, or BA). Build SES terciles from the full sample (cuts at -0.340 and +0.227). Compute per-bin Wilson 95% CIs for BA rates by race; compute Black-White and Black-vs-non-Black gaps with race-stratified bootstrap CIs (B=2000). Flag cells with N<25 or events<5 as UNSTABLE (one cell: Low-SES Black, k=4). Repeat gap analysis at quartiles, quintiles, ±1 SD, and deciles for sensitivity. Fit logistic regression BA ~ race × SES_tercile + female + ASVAB-composite + percentile-in-class + family_size as a robustness check only. Deliver the hypothesis in two readings: (a) descriptive - no Black advantage in any SES bin, gap largest and most precisely-estimated at low SES; (b) covariate-adjusted - within-bin Black advantage at mid and high SES, most pronounced at mid SES (interaction p=0.042).
